Acceptance check: in a chest-height shot at 1280x720 with the man filling about 40% of the frame, the face must show skin micro-detail (pores, stubble or creases, uneven tone, no uniform waxy orange cast) and an expression readable from the brows, eyes and mouth. The hair must break into strands with a soft hairline, not a sculpted shell. The shirt must show a visible fabric texture or pattern, legible seams, pockets and buttons, and at least 4-5 distinct folds where the cloth bears load (elbows, waist, collar). The hand must show articulated fingers actually gripping the weapon. That is the level of A's flannel, denim and face.

No game code or assets were edited.. Judge: A wins all four pairs clearly, and none is close to indistinguishable. The A frames have deliberate cinematic composition, dense set dressing that tells a story, high-fidelity character materials (cloth weave, folds, skin and facial detail, readable expressions) and natural poses that carry weight. The B frames are all the same avatar on the same plaza, and they share the same problems. The character is mid-poly, with waxy orange skin, a blank face, hair that reads as a solid shell and flat cloth. The locomotion poses are stiff: the walk has near-locked knees, a short stride and arms held in front of the body, and the run is a legs-together hop with the forearms parked in front of the chest and a shadow that does not meet the feet. The foreground is a big empty plaza of repeating large tiles with blotchy stain decals, the image is soft and low-contrast under warm haze, and the street-name text spills past its sign plate. B's background architecture (brutalist car-park block, glass towers, shophouses, planters, van) is its strongest element, but it is distant and almost unpopulated. Ranked by how much of the gap each fix would close: (1) poses, so the run has a split stride, forward lean and arms pumping opposite the legs, and the walk shows a planted heel, a flexed stance knee, a narrow track and relaxed arm swing; (2) character shading and cloth detail; (3) a populated foreground and plaza (pedestrians, props, nearby traffic) plus stronger key-light contrast. Only A in pairs 1 and 4 genuinely wowed. No B frame did.
